title: Minneapolis City Council fails to override mayor's veto on driverless vehicle ordinance
key_facts: A vote to override Mayor Jacob Frey's veto of the 'Workers Drive Minneapolis' ordinance failed 7-5 on Thursday 15 Oct 2026.
The ordinance, passed 1 Oct, would require a human monitor in driverless vehicles.
Frey vetoed it the next day, calling it a 'back-door ban' and citing benefits for people with disabilities.
Waymo called it 'a de facto ban on autonomous vehicles' and said it operates in 15 cities with nothing like it.
Councilmembers Robin Wonsley, Jamal Osman, Jason Chavez and Aurin Chowdhury said they will restart the legislative process.
St. Paul's council passed a resolution to study the impact on workforce and safety.
quote_evidence: A vote to override Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey's veto of the City Council's rideshare ordinance that would require a human monitor in driverless vehicles failed Thursday morning at City Hall on a 7-5 vote.
After the vote, Wonsley, Osman, Chavez and Chowdhury said they would be restarting the legislative process to regulate driverless vehicles.
Waymo officials echoed Frey's concerns earlier this month, calling the ordinance "a de facto ban on autonomous vehicles,"
why_it_matters_hint: The first US attempt to require a human in driverless taxis is stalled, but its backers will try again.
notes: Follow-up to the 15 Oct edition (C11-18, FOX 9): the override vote that was due on 15 Oct has now failed.
